But careful: `for other in items: adj[other].discard(var)` then the clique fill. Note that `adj[x].add(y)` where y in items — fine ✓. But note `neigh` (== adj[var]) is not modified by those adds... `adj[items[i]].add(items[j])` — items[i] != var since var ∉ neigh ✓. OK.

Wait, one thing: is `adj[var]` guaranteed to contain only *live* variables? When var' is eliminated earlier, we do `adj[other].discard(var')` for all other in adj[var'] — so var' is removed from all its neighbors' sets ✓, and any node that had var' as a neighbor loses it ✓. And nodes not adjacent to var' don't have it. ✓ So adj[x] always contains only live nodes ✓. Good.

4. `build_plan`: `involved` computed by scanning all factor scopes each step: O(m + steps) per step → fine.

Let me now also double check `build_plan`'s handling of a factor whose scope contains var multiple times — impossible ✓.
